title: Internal Hom from a strictly perfect complex
statement: Let U be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let P be a strictly perfect bounded complex of finite projective O_U-modules [def-pc-perfect-complex]. For every complex M of O_U-modules, the derived internal Hom R\mathcal Hom_{O_U}(P,M) [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] is represented by the ordinary Hom complex \mathcal Hom^\bullet_{O_U}(P,M), and the canonical comparison from the ordinary Hom complex to derived internal Hom is an isomorphism.

proof.text: By def-pc-perfect-complex, each term of P retracts from a finite free module and P is bounded. Apply lem-sc-finite-free-internal-hom-exact to a short exact sequence. Contravariant precomposition with the retraction and inclusion gives a retract of short complexes; homology, monomorphisms and epimorphisms are preserved by retracts, so internal Hom from each term preserves short exact sequences.

Apply lem-pc-bounded-exact-term-hom-quasi-iso to the quasi-isomorphism from M to its functorial K-injective replacement. The Hom complex of def-pur-hom-complex therefore maps by a quasi-isomorphism to the Hom complex of the replacement. Localization inverts this map.

The comparison theorem of def-pur-derived-internal-hom identifies the localized Hom complex of the replacement with derived internal Hom. Compose its inverse component with the isomorphism just obtained. The same quasi-isomorphism argument proves the comparison for every functorial K-injective replacement.
